archetype: Mono-red Goblin swarm built around Zada's copy hub (v1.2.0). The floor is bodies plus per-creature cantrips. The ceiling is a one-turn copy of the whole board or a storm turn. Since storm-tune-v1 it carries a real protection package for Zada and cheap two-class interaction, and no mass land denial at bracket 3

role_assignment.default_role: A swarm that leans beatdown and paces toward one burst turn through Zada. You set the role per seat, and you ask again every turn cycle (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Against slower engine decks you are the beatdown. Goldfish: an early token maker is drawn by mean turn 3.09, 68.9% of games by turn 6. The unopposed one-seat clock is median turn 8 (48.5% by turn 8, 4.9% by turn 6). That clock comes from a model with no blockers and no removal, so it is optimistic. A deck you cannot out-race pushes you into the control seat. The v1.2.0 adds are made for that seat: two redirects, two artifact answers and a punisher. Use them on the piece that beats you, not on whatever looks scary (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy).
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: There are three triggers, and you need only one. (a) Zada on the battlefield with a cantrip to cast at her. Goldfish group 'Zada online with a cantrip drawn': 83.0% of runs, 67.3% by turn 6, mean turn 4.92. Commander cast at mean turn 4.11, median 4, 94.8% by turn 6. Verified stacks 001 and 003 are the payload. (b) A storm payoff plus a ritual. 21.0% of runs, only 7.4% by turn 6, mean turn 6.9. No commander needed: stack 002 resolves off Impact Tremors and stack 004 has Zada in the command zone. (c) New in v1.2.0: a creature-copy spell (Heat Shimmer, Molten Duplication, Twinflame, Electroduplicate) cast at Zada alone over a wide board. It is not a declared goldfish target, so it has no measured rate. Verified stack 017: Heat Shimmer at Zada alone, with three other creatures out, makes three hasty copies, and the Zada token is lost to the legend rule. The board ends at 8 creatures, 3 of them hasty. Fire when the table's instant-speed interaction is spent. Better still, fire with one of Deflecting Swat, Untimely Malfunction, Plaza of Heroes or Hexing Squelcher already available, so one answer cannot fizzle the whole turn. A sweeper you can see coming forces the half-go: take the cards or the wide hasty board now (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math).

engines.piece: Zada, Hedron Grinder + the cantrip set
engines.engine: The copy hub. An instant or sorcery that targets only Zada is copied once for each other creature you control that it could target. Cast a cantrip at her and every body draws a card. By oracle text the deck has eight instants and sorceries that target one creature and draw: Accelerate, Ancestral Anger, Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Fists of Flame, Impolite Entrance, Might of the Meek, Renegade Tactics. Fists of Flame is the closer: each copy resolves after more draws, so the trample buff grows with each one.
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 (four Goblin tokens plus one-mana Crimson Wisps at Zada draws five cards and gives the team haste) and verified stack 003 (Fists of Flame sizes each buff in sequence); oracle text for the set

engines.piece: Heat Shimmer / Molten Duplication / Twinflame / Electroduplicate at Zada
engines.engine: The v1.2.0 ceiling. Each of these copies one target creature, with haste. Cast at Zada alone, Zada's trigger gives one copy per other creature you control, so the board doubles for a turn, with haste. The original resolves last on Zada, and the legend rule removes the Zada token it makes, so the copy count is the number of OTHER creatures you control. Every copy is an entry, so Purphoros (2 to each opponent), Impact Tremors (1) and General Kreat (1) fire once per copy, and ETB bodies (Goblin Instigator, Mogg War Marshal, Siege-Gang Commander) make tokens again. Heat Shimmer's copies are exiled at the end step, so no dies trigger fires. That makes them free fodder for Goblin Bombardment before they go. Molten Duplication's copies are also artifacts, which pumps Storm-Kiln Artist. Twinflame's strive cost is irrelevant when its one target is Zada.
engines.evidence: verified stack 017 (checker pass, iteration 2): Heat Shimmer cast at Zada alone with Mogg War Marshal and two Goblin tokens out gets three copies, one per other creature. They make three hasty token copies, and the Mogg War Marshal copy's enters trigger adds a fourth Goblin. The Zada token goes to the legend rule. Result: 8 creatures, 3 with haste, 6 attack power available that turn. The three copies are exiled at the end step and no dies trigger fires. The other three spells' versions, and the converter totals, rest on oracle text; combo_details by_card shows no line contained in this deck

engines.piece: Ancestors' Aid / Reckless Ransacking / Sudden Breakthrough at Zada
engines.engine: Pump spells that make a Treasure, so on Zada they are rituals. Each copy that resolves should make its own Treasure: about one mana per other creature for {1}{R}, enough to fund the rest of the burst turn. With Storm-Kiln Artist out, magecraft ('cast or copy') adds another Treasure per copy.
engines.evidence: oracle text; the goldfish names Ancestors' Aid, Reckless Ransacking and Sudden Breakthrough under treasure_sources_not_modelled, so the hoard figure (mean 10.08 Treasures by turn 10) undercounts them

engines.piece: Empty the Warrens + Impact Tremors + Grapeshot
engines.engine: The storm half, which does not need Zada. Storm tokens become each-opponent damage through the entry converters, and Grapeshot reads the same storm count. General Kreat and Purphoros are the same entry trigger on other permanents, and Purphoros pays 2 per entry.
engines.evidence: verified stack 002: Empty the Warrens cast as the fourth spell gets 3 storm copies, 8 Goblin tokens enter, Impact Tremors deals 8 to each opponent, and a later Grapeshot sees storm count 4. Every card on that board and in that graveyard is in v1.2.0

engines.piece: Battle Hymn / Brightstone Ritual / Three Tree City / Skirk Prospector
engines.engine: Mana that scales with bodies, not lands. Battle Hymn adds {R} per creature, Brightstone Ritual {R} per Goblin, Three Tree City (naming Goblin) adds mana equal to your Goblins, and Skirk Prospector turns Goblins into {R}. A wide board is the mana for its own payoff turn.
engines.evidence: oracle text; goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn['5'] = 4.69 with land_drop_hit_rate_by_turn['5'] = 0.719. Model coverage reads Three Tree City only as a mana land, so whether its scaling is priced was not confirmed

engines.piece: Krenko, Mob Boss + Skirk Prospector + Goblin Warchief
engines.engine: A bounded burst, not a loop. Krenko with haste taps the turn he lands for a token per Goblin, and Prospector turns the tokens into one-shot red mana for a payoff already in hand. combo_details lists this trio and a Goblin Chieftain variant as infinite, but both records assume Krenko is the commander.
engines.evidence: verified stack 004: Zada is the commander, so a sacrificed Krenko stays in the graveyard and the line ends after one activation. bracket_report excludes both records for the commander assumption (CR 903.9a)

engines.piece: Goblin Bombardment + Skullclamp + Pashalik Mons + Rundvelt Hordemaster
engines.engine: Free-outlet conversion. Bombardment turns any body into a point of damage at instant speed, in response to removal or a sweeper, and it is where the end-of-turn copies go before they leave. Skullclamp turns a 1/1 into two cards for {1}. Pashalik Mons and Rundvelt Hordemaster pay out on each Goblin death. A swept board still becomes damage and cards.
engines.evidence: oracle text for all four; the goldfish names Skullclamp as draw it does not model, so its card advantage is not in mean_extra_cards_drawn_by_turn

engines.piece: Swiftfoot Boots + Hexing Squelcher + Deflecting Swat + Untimely Malfunction + Plaza of Heroes
engines.engine: Zada's protection package, which was the pilot's main v1.2.0 push. It covers both kinds in the doc's taxonomy. Always-on: Boots give hexproof and haste, Squelcher gives Zada 'Ward—Pay 2 life' and stops your spells from being countered, so the payload resolves. Single-use: Deflecting Swat is free while you control a commander and changes the targets of a spell or ability. Untimely Malfunction changes the target of a single-target spell. Plaza of Heroes exiles itself to give hexproof and indestructible, which also covers destroy and damage sweepers. Hexproof from Boots and ward stop only opponents, so neither one blocks your own cantrips at Zada.
engines.evidence: oracle text for all five; deck-audit protection axis reads 6 copies, 'at' the 5-7 target. That count includes Purphoros and Roaming Throne, which protect only themselves, and leaves out Plaza of Heroes as possibly uncounted. By oracle text, five cards protect Zada

engines.piece: Abrade / Untimely Malfunction / Harsh Mentor / Blasphemous Act
engines.engine: The interaction suite. Abrade and Untimely Malfunction are modal, cheap and instant: creature or artifact removal, and a redirect or 'can't block' when nothing needs killing. Harsh Mentor deals 2 to an opponent each time they activate a non-mana ability of an artifact, creature or land, a tax on every seat's engines. Blasphemous Act is the reset button, and it is nearly free against a wide table.
engines.evidence: oracle text; deck-audit interaction 10 copies 'at' the target of 8 (suite 14); interaction-breadth 2 classes (creature, artifact), with enchantment, graveyard and land uncovered; goldfish interaction_castable_by_turn['6'] = 0.235 (a floor, since the model never holds mana up)

engines.engine: A rebuild that costs a land slot, not a spell slot. Channel makes two hasty 1/1 Spirits at instant speed after a sweeper, and costs {1} less per legendary creature you control. The Spirits are also two more bodies for Zada's copies and Battle Hymn.

candidate_missing_lines.title: A creature-copy spell at Zada with Purphoros and Impact Tremors out
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: Stack 017 verified the copy count, one per other creature. By oracle text, each token copy is a creature entering, so Purphoros (2) and Impact Tremors (1) should each trigger per copy against every opponent. The copies are sacrificed at the next end step anyway, so Bombardment can cash them in first. The per-opponent total for an N-creature board, and whether copies of ETB token makers add more entries, are what a scenario must count

candidate_missing_lines.title: Molten Duplication at Zada with Storm-Kiln Artist: artifact copies and a Treasure per copy
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: oracle text: Storm-Kiln Artist's magecraft fires on 'cast or copy' and it gets +1/+0 per artifact you control. Molten Duplication's copies are artifacts. The Treasure count, the Artist's final power, and whether the Artist's own copy has magecraft for the rest of the turn are open

candidate_missing_lines.title: Treasure pump spells at Zada as a ritual into a storm payoff
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: oracle text: each copy that resolves makes a Treasure, and Storm-Kiln adds one per copy. The copies are not cast, so they do not raise Grapeshot's storm count. Stack 002 established that rule for storm copies (CR 707.10). Whether the mana nets enough casts to make Grapeshot lethal is the question

candidate_missing_lines.title: Past in Flames rebuilds the ritual and copy chain for a second payoff
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: combo_details by_card returns no record for Past in Flames. Oracle text gives every instant and sorcery in the graveyard flashback at its mana cost, and since v1.2.0 that includes the copy spells as well as the rituals. Recast spells raise the storm count again. Whether the mana nets out and what count the second payoff sees are open

candidate_missing_lines.title: Roaming Throne naming Goblin doubles Zada's copy trigger
candidate_missing_lines.why_plausible: oracle text: Zada is a Goblin and her copy ability is a triggered ability. Roaming Throne makes a triggered ability of another creature of the chosen type trigger an additional time. Whether the second trigger makes a second full set of copies, and what those copies target, is unresolved

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Assume the wrath: over a four-player game one is near-certain, so deploy in waves and keep a rebuild in hand (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). This deck buys resilience, not restraint. Goblin Bombardment cashes the board in response, Skullclamp makes the deaths into cards, Mogg War Marshal and Pashalik Mons leave bodies behind, and Sokenzan rebuilds two hasty bodies at instant speed. Plaza of Heroes can make Zada indestructible against a destroy or damage sweeper. Against control, holding back IS the loss. A sweeper you can see coming forces the half-go: fire the cantrip engine and bank the cards (strategy:critical-mass.storm-math).
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes hit this deck's velocity directly. The plan is several one- and two-mana spells a turn, so recount your hand under the tax before you commit (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). You will not own the long game under a lock, so you are the beatdown racing its completion (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Name the out early: Abrade and Untimely Malfunction answer an artifact lock piece, and Harsh Mentor punishes non-mana activations. Nothing in the list answers an enchantment, which is deck-audit's uncovered class and the honest exposure here. No mass land denial, by the bracket-3 choice (strategy:deckbuilding.power-level.barometers).
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Take the control seat. Your bodies replace themselves and theirs do not. Goldfish mean bodies are 2.82 by turn 5 and 4.78 by turn 6, enough to block while the engine sets up. Blasphemous Act costs {1} less per creature on the battlefield and is near-free against a wide table. Abrade, Goblin Bombardment and Siege-Gang Commander pick off attackers. Rank by clock, not by how scary it looks (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy), and let 40 life absorb the early turns.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Held answers rot against combo: the last profitable moment is now (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Rank how close they are to combo above every board threat. v1.2.0 gives you stack interaction for the first time. Deflecting Swat (free while you control a commander) and Untimely Malfunction can redirect a targeted combo piece or tutor ability. Harsh Mentor punishes activated-ability engines. Hexing Squelcher wins the counter war on your own burst. None of it stops a combo that targets nothing, so pressure their setup turn rather than plan to out-race a dedicated combo deck. Your storm assembly is a 21.0% line (mean turn 6.9), a ceiling and not a clock.

distribution_notes: The curve is low: 17 one-drops, 26 twos, 11 threes, 7 fours, 2 fives and one nine (Blasphemous Act, which costs less per creature). Modal mana value is 2 across 64 nonland entries (deck-facts). Mana: 36 land copies across 15 entries. 32 red sources against a Karsten target of 22. Two lands always enter tapped and three conditionally. 40 counted against Burgess's 36 with the persistent producers. Deck-audit reads mana-base, mana-sources, taplands, colour-sources and consistency all 'at'. Creatures: 25. Under target: card-advantage (4 counted against 10, but 11 cards the taxonomy cannot read, including the whole cantrip set, are uncounted), threat-density (1 against 3), sweepers (0, although Blasphemous Act's oracle text is a sweeper; the taxonomy tags it removal:damage) and interaction-breadth (2 of 5 classes). Over target: ramp (13 against 10-12), which is the ritual and Treasure base. Protection is 6, 'at' 5-7. Speed: keep-first-seven 78.7%, mean mulligans 0.255, commander mean cast turn 4.11 (median 4, 94.8% by turn 6), available mana 4.69 on turn 5 with land-drop hit rate down to 71.9%. The burst turns are funded by rituals, not lands. The three declared engines: Zada plus a cantrip 83.0% (8 cards, thinnest component), early token maker 82.8% (7 cards), storm payoff plus ritual 21.0% (two 2-card components, both flagged thin). The storm line is an AND of two thin draws, which is why it sits at a fifth of runs. On the redundancy table (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors), 7-8 copies is about 41% of openers. Paired against the v1.1.1 list on the same 10,000 seeds (storm-tune-v1 net_change), the merge traded early tempo for late reach: killed by T6 0.057 to 0.047 and by T10 0.901 to 0.850, board power at T6 down 1.00. Damage at T10 rose +27.3 [16.1, 38.5], extra cards by T8 +0.75, interaction affordable at T6 +0.040, all Holm-significant. The pre-registered kill_by_8 objective was NOT met (0.485 against 0.62). The goldfish cannot see Abrade, Deflecting Swat, Untimely Malfunction, Swiftfoot Boots, Skullclamp, Blasphemous Act or Past in Flames (model-coverage: invisible), so the protection and interaction this merge bought show up only as their mana cost.
overall_assessment: v1.2.0 is still a linear deck in Duke's sense: every card feeds one threshold, and the deck's defense is speed, redundancy and resilience (strategy:critical-mass). What changed is how the deck pays for its single hub. Before, it kept a second copy hub as a backup. Now it protects Zada: five cards stop or fizzle a removal spell aimed at her, and Hexing Squelcher makes your own payload uncounterable. This is the doc's insurance trade for an engine that runs through the commander (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance). Always-on protection goes down early. A held redirect covers the pivot turn, and Deflecting Swat costs no held mana at all while she is on the board. The median game is the swarm plus the Zada cantrip engine: bodies by turn 3, Zada at turn 4, then a card per body for one red (verified stacks 001 and 003). The ceiling has moved. The buyback loop left in v1.1.0 on purpose to sit at true bracket 3, and the list now holds two bounded ceilings and no infinite. One is the storm turn (verified stack 002, without Zada). The other is a creature-copy spell at Zada that doubles a wide board with haste and fires every entry converter once per copy. That second ceiling is now verified for its core step (stack 017). Heat Shimmer at Zada alone over three other creatures leaves 8 creatures, 3 of them hasty, and the Zada token goes to the legend rule. What it pays through Purphoros, Impact Tremors and Storm-Kiln Artist is still a candidate. The halves still stand apart. Only one declared engine needs the commander, and stacks 002 and 004 resolve without Zada on the battlefield, so killing the hub costs you the draw engine, not the kill. Against three seats, raw burn does not add up to ~120 life, so the payoffs that count hit every seat at once: Purphoros, Impact Tremors and General Kreat on each entry, Grapeshot off the storm count, a wide hasty alpha (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry, strategy:conversion.entries-vs-deaths). The new interaction is cheap, modal and two-class (creature and artifact). It suits the 1-to-3 economy: hold it until the threat points at you or the combo is one piece away (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Enchantments and graveyards stay unanswered, and that is the next gap to price (strategy:deckbuilding.interaction-suite). Politically the board reads as 1/1s until the turn it wins. Play Krenko, Storm-Kiln Artist and the copy spells after the table's removal is spent (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection). Mulligan to the enabler class, a body maker plus a cantrip or ritual (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands). Commit fully only when the table's open interaction is counted and one of your redirects is live (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). The goldfish measured the merge as slower to an early kill and stronger late. It cannot see the protection and interaction the merge was for, so the DeckCheck Interaction and Resilience groups are the readings to watch. The last scan (2026-10-20, an older list) graded I1 C, I2 F, S1 C, S2 B, S3 B, and no scan of v1.2.0 exists yet.
gaps: No section on one-turn creature-copy spells (Heat Shimmer, Molten Duplication, Twinflame, Electroduplicate): copying a board for a single turn, entries vs bodies, the legend rule on a copied legend (stack 017 shows the cost: the Zada copy is lost), and how a one-turn hasty board changes the alpha-strike and sweeper math. strategy:conversion.entries-vs-deaths prices the entries but not the copy effect

No section on redirect effects (Deflecting Swat, Untimely Malfunction) as dual-use cards that protect your engine and also disrupt an opponent's targeted spell or ability. strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance names single-use instants generically but not redirection's other half
No section on punisher creatures that tax opponents' activations (Harsh Mentor). strategy:conversion.passive-tax covers upkeep-triggered each-opponent taxation only
No goad or forced-combat section: Grenzo, Havoc Raiser compels a creature to attack elsewhere, which takes away the choice rather than persuading; strategy:multiplayer.politics does not cover it
